title: Epistolae Prima Classis
author: Ambrose
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0022.stoa009.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Promisisti te con« flictaturum, promisisti e te allaturum aut accepta< turum esse rationem. Libenter itaque accepimus < praefationem tuam. Optavimus ut quasi christianus < venires. Obtuli tibi epistolam Arii, quam scripsit < Arius, de cujus nomine dicitis vos injuriam fre- < quenter sustinere. Dicitis quod Arium non sequa< mini. Hodie aperta debet esse sententia : aut cont demna illum, aut astrue f quibusvis lectionibus.
passages.english: You promised that you would debate; you promised that you would either give or accept a reasoned account. So we gladly accepted your preface. We wished that you would come as a Christian. I offered you the letter of Arius, which Arius wrote, on account of whose name you say that you frequently suffer injury. You say that you do not follow Arius. Today your opinion must be open: either condemn him, or defend [him] with whatever readings [of Scripture] you please.
passages.notes: The '<' marks and stray letters ('e', 'f', 't') are quotation and footnote marks from the printed edition and have been left out. 'astrue' is taken as 'defend, support'.

passages.original: i3. Ambrosius episcopus dixit: < Omni ore con- I demnatio facta est in eum, qui negaret Dei Filium < sempiternum. Negavit Arius; hunc sequitur Palla. dius, qui non vult condemnare 790 Arium. Itac que utrum hujus probanda sententia sit, conside- I rate : et utrum secundum Scripturas dicat, aut < contra Scripturas, intelligere licet. Lectum est < enim : Sempiterna virlut Dei alque divinilas.
passages.english: 13. Bishop Ambrose said: "With every voice condemnation has been pronounced against anyone who would deny that the Son of God is everlasting. Arius denied [it]; Palladius follows him, since he will not condemn Arius. So consider whether his opinion is to be approved; and one may understand whether he speaks according to the Scriptures or against the Scriptures. For it has been read: 'The everlasting power of God and [his] divinity.'
passages.notes: '790' is a page or column number from the printed edition and has been omitted. 'virlut ... alque' read as 'virtus ... atque' (Rom. 1:20).

passages.original: 14. Eusebius episcopus dixit : < Specialilcr dicit solum Patrem sempiternum, et Filium aliquando coepisse. >
passages.english: 14. Bishop Eusebius said: "He specifically says that only the Father is everlasting, and that the Son began at some point."

passages.original: Eusebius episcopus dixit : < Quid superfluis immoraris? Cum legeretur impietas Arii, qui hoc dicit de Patre, quia solus habet immortalitatem , anulisti testimonium ad consensum impietatis Arii , ex Apostolo dicens : Qui solus habet immortalitatem , et lucem inaccessibilem habitat (I Tim. VI, 16). Sed si intelligis, tulius naturae dignitatem, in Dei nomine expressit: Siquidem in Dei nomine Pater et Filius designantur. >
passages.english: Bishop Eusebius said: "Why do you dwell on superfluous things? When the impiety of Arius was being read, who says this of the Father, that he alone has immortality, you brought forward testimony in agreement with the impiety of Arius, quoting from the Apostle: 'Who alone has immortality, and dwells in unapproachable light' (1 Tim. 6:16). But if you understand [it], he expressed the dignity of the whole nature in the name of God, since in the name of God the Father and the Son are designated."
passages.notes: 'anulisti' read as 'attulisti' (you brought forward); 'tulius' read as 'totius' (of the whole). Both emendations are uncertain.

passages.original: 62. e Felix episcopus Jadertinus dixit: < Palladium, qui blasphemias dicit in Filium sicut Arius, cum omnibus pariter condemno. >
passages.english: 62. Felix, bishop of Iader, said: "Together with all, I condemn Palladius, who utters blasphemies against the Son as Arius does."
passages.notes: Jadertinus: of Iader (Zadar). The stray 'e' is a footnote mark and has been omitted.

passages.original: Secundianus dixit : < Quis fuerit Arius, ignoro : quid dixerit nescio. Mecum loqueris vivus ad vivum. Illud dico quod Christus dixit: i Unigenitum qui eat in sinu Patris (Joan. I, 18); ergo unigenitum Filium se asserii Patris : Filius igitur unigenitus est Dei ' Filius verus.
passages.english: Secundianus said: "Who Arius was, I do not know; what he said, I do not know. You are speaking with me, a living man to a living man. I say what Christ said: 'the only-begotten, who is in the bosom of the Father' (John 1:18). Therefore he declared himself the only-begotten Son of the Father; so the only-begotten Son is the true Son of God."
passages.notes: 'eat' read as 'est', 'asserii' as 'asseruit'. The citation is from John's Gospel, not Christ's own words; the text has it so.

passages.original: Denique cum viderent se Arii epistolæ sacrile- , giis perurgeri (quam ideo subdidimus, ut eam etiam vestra dementia perhorresceret), resilientes e de media epistolae lectione, petierunt ut eurum propositis responderemus. Quamquam non esset ordinis nequc rationis, ut proposita interrumperemus; responsumque esset a nobis ut damnarent Arii impietates, et de quibus vellent, ordine, locoque servato, f eorum intentionibus responderemuS : tamen acquievimus praeposterae voluntati. Ibi tum Evangelii scripta talsames, proposuerunt nobis, dixisse Dominum : Qui me misit, major me est ;
passages.english: Then, when they saw themselves hard pressed by the sacrileges of Arius's letter (which we have therefore appended, so that your Clemency also might shudder at it), they sprang back from the middle of the reading of the letter and asked that we answer their propositions. It was not according to order or reason that we should interrupt the matters put forward, and our reply had been that they should condemn the impieties of Arius, and that we would answer their contentions on whatever points they wished, keeping to order and sequence. Nevertheless we gave in to their preposterous wish. Then, falsifying the writings of the Gospel, they put it to us that the Lord had said: 'He who sent me is greater than I';
passages.notes: 'dementia' (madness) is evidently a misreading of 'clementia' (Clemency), a title of address for the emperors, and is translated so. 'talsames' read as 'falsantes' (falsifying). This is uncertain.

passages.original: Quæsisti a me utrum anima caelestis esse videatur substantiæ;d non enim aut922sanguinem, aut ignem, aut nervorum harmoniam animam putas, ut vulgus philosophorum interpretatur : aut, ut illa patricia quædam eorum prosapia Platonis disputat, quod ipsum se movet, et uon movetur ab alio, ipsa tibi anima videtur : vel certe III Aristoteles acri ingenio quintum quoddam elementi genus induxit, probasti, id est ἐντελέχειαν, ex quo componeres et velut fingeres animæ substantiam.
passages.english: You have asked me whether the soul seems to be of heavenly substance. For you do not think the soul is blood, or fire, or a harmony of the sinews, as the common run of philosophers interprets it; nor does the soul seem to you to be that which moves itself and is not moved by another, as that patrician lineage of theirs, [the school] of Plato, argues; nor indeed have you approved the fifth kind of element which Aristotle, with his keen intellect, introduced, that is, *entelecheia* [actuality], from which you might compose and, as it were, fashion the substance of the soul.
passages.notes: The passage is garbled in places. The "d" after "substantiæ", the "922" (probably a page or column number) and the "III" are taken as stray marks and left untranslated. "uon" is read as "non". The syntax around "probasti" is loose. I have taken it as "nor have you approved", but the edition's punctuation is uncertain.

passages.original: Vercellensem Ecclesiam episcopo propter intestinas contentiones diutius orbatam delens, concordiam qua Eusebius olim fuerat electus , laudat ; vique Christum in medio nri stantem habere eadem Eeclesia studeat, suadet. Hine invekitur ire Sarmationem et Barbatianum , qui e monasterio profugi, abstinentiam ac virginitatemqua abjecerant, aliis.
passages.english: Lamenting that the Church of Vercelli has long been deprived of a bishop because of internal quarrels, he praises the concord by which Eusebius had once been elected. He urges that the same Church strive to have Christ standing in our midst. Then he inveighs against Sarmatio and Barbatianus, who, having fled from the monastery, [begrudged] others the abstinence and virginity which they themselves had cast off.
passages.notes: This is an editorial summary (argumentum) of the letter, not Ambrose's own text. Scanning errors read as follows: "delens" as "dolens", "vique" as "utque", "nri" as "nostri", "Hine invekitur ire" as "Hinc invehitur in", and "virginitatemqua" as "virginitatem quam". The sentence finishes with "invidebant" in the following context, and the bracketed verb is supplied from there.

passages.original: Denique sanctus DIonysius exegit votis, ut in exsilio vitam poneret; ne regressus confusa institutis seu usu infidelium studia plebis aut cleri inveniret : meruitque hanc gratiam ; ut pacem Domini tranquillo affectu secum referret. Itaque ut Eusebius sanctus prior levavit vexillum confessionis; ita beatus Dionysius in exsilii locis i priori martyribus Undo vitam exhalavit.
passages.english: Finally, holy Dionysius asked in his prayers that he might lay down his life in exile, so that on returning he would not find the people's or the clergy's pursuits thrown into confusion by the practices or customs of unbelievers. He was granted this grace, that he took the peace of the Lord with him in a tranquil disposition. And so, as holy Eusebius first raised the banner of confession, so blessed Dionysius breathed out his life in the places of exile with a title higher than [that of] the earlier martyrs.
passages.notes: "i priori martyribus Undo" is corrupt. It is read tentatively as "priore martyribus titulo" ("with a title higher than the martyrs"), and the sense is uncertain. The phrase "confusa institutis seu usu infidelium" is also somewhat obscure.
